Labels to remember

PASSIVE actor missing or last · SHALL duty, future or permission? · DOUBLET two or more words for one idea · BLOAT words that add nothing · NEGATIVE stacked not/no · VAGUE no measurable standard · OLD WORD hereinafter, herein · HIDDEN VERB the action buried in a noun

SUGGESTED DRAFTING · plain English, same purpose. Use it as feedback on how you organised the clause.

16.1 Each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement and the Call-Offs is limited, for each Call-Off, to 100% of the Contract Price of that Call-Off, with a minimum of EUR 11,000,000. This limit is subject to Clause 16.5 (Protected Liabilities).

15 If Meridian does not achieve Final Acceptance by the date in the Call-Off, as adjusted under Clause 8, it must pay GER delay damages of EUR 25,000 for each day of delay. Total delay damages under a Call-Off must not exceed 10% of its Contract Price. The Parties agree that this rate is a genuine pre-estimate of GER’s likely loss, based on the assumptions recorded in the Call-Off. Subject to Clause 16.5, delay damages are GER’s only monetary remedy for that delay. GER must not recover twice for the same loss.

20 GER may end a Call-Off for convenience by giving Meridian 90 days' written notice. GER must pay for conforming Work performed, approved non-cancellable commitments and reasonable documented demobilisation costs, less avoided costs and amounts already paid. GER does not pay profit on unperformed Work.

Check: every number from the notes appears once; "roughly", "or so", "probably" and "and stuff like that" are gone; the clauses say who pays, the carve-out in 16.5 is kept and the same loss cannot be paid twice; each sentence has an actor and a "must" or "may". These numbers come from the role-play, not from D3.

CLAUSE PROFILE · D3 clauses 15, 16.1 and 20 (the three negotiated clauses)

What it is and its job. Delay damages price the delay in advance; the cap limits what either party can claim; termination for convenience lets GER leave a Call-Off.

What it should contain. A rate and a cap for delay damages and the milestones they apply to; the amount and base of the liability cap; the notice period and the payments due on convenience termination.

Why it matters in Project Horizon. They are the money and exit clauses of the framework: what a delay costs, how much anyone can lose, and what it costs GER to walk away.

How it relates to the other contracts. D3 gives GER, as Operator, the right to charge the Contract Price to the Joint Account (clause 1): PETROX bears 40% of what GER agrees here. A cap in D3 does not limit what PETROX can claim from GER under D2 Article 10 (USD 25,000,000).

SHAPING THE EXERCISE · what to ask while they organize

Ask: Which vague word hides a number or a rule? (roughly, or so, probably, stuff).

Ask: Who must do what in clause 15? (Meridian pays; GER recovers).

Ask: Does anything in your clause change D3 15 or 16? (flag it: negotiated numbers are a deal change, not a drafting change).

Now that you can write a deal, the question is how to keep writing clearly when nobody is checking. Three habits.

C. Habits of clear communication

TRANSITION

"A course lasts six days. A habit lasts years. Three habits: know where to look when you doubt, edit your own text before anyone sees it, and take criticism as information."

DoubtBest source

Source. Garner, Legal Writing in Plain English (third edition) is in your files. Recommend it as the first stop for style questions. Do not quote it in class beyond a line: refer participants to the book.

The rule. A reliable source is one you can name, date and show to a colleague. "I read it somewhere" is not a source.

Ex 6.8Edit yourself · the old-words hunt10 minFRAMEWORK · D3

First the six steps. Then compare an old-style sentence with its plain version and answer the questions.

Six steps for editing your own text

  1. Read it aloud. Where do you run out of breath?
  2. Who must do what? Put the actor first.
  3. Cut doublets, bloat and old words.
  4. Check numbers, dates and defined terms against the other documents.
  5. Leave it for an hour (or a night) and read again.
  6. Ask one person to read it and say what it means.
Original · old-style wording

WITNESSETH: That the party of the first part, hereinafter referred to as the Seller, in consideration of the sum aforesaid, doth hereby agree to deliver the goods herein described, and this Agreement shall be null and void in the event that the Buyer fails to pay. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have hereunto set their hands.

Plain English · same deal

The Seller agrees to deliver the goods described in this Agreement for the price stated above. This Agreement ends automatically if the Buyer does not pay. The parties sign below.

Tick the old words that can go without changing the meaning.
✓ Five can go. “Null and void” and the payment trigger carry the deal: they must stay in some form. Cut the ornament, not the meaning.
The plain version says the Agreement “ends automatically” if the Buyer does not pay. The Seller wants the choice to end it or not. Which sentence gives that?
✗ It states no consequence.
✗ Not quite. Look again.
✗ It still ends the contract without a choice.
✓ “Null and void” and “ends automatically” take the choice away from the Seller. “May end” gives a right and changes the deal: ask the client which one is wanted before you choose.
TEACHER NOTE

The old words come from the NDA reference sheet (archaic expressions such as "in witness whereof"). Ask participants to add one from their own work. Then the trap: replacing "null and void" with a right to terminate changes who decides.

Ex 6.9Accepting constructive criticism10 minFRAMEWORK · D3

Tick the comments that help you improve. Then fix one that does not.

Tick the comments that are constructive.
✓ Three are constructive: they point at the text, say what is wrong or right and what to do. The others judge the writer or say nothing useful.
Which rewrite turns "This is confusing" into a useful comment?
✗ Not quite. Look again.
✗ It says nothing about where or how.
✗ It is an opinion about the writer's work, not a way to improve it.
✓ A good comment names the place, says what you could not do, and asks for a change.
TEACHER NOTE

Receiving criticism. Three questions for the writer: What did the reader understand? Which part did not work? What can I change in one minute? Do not defend the text: ask. Pairs swap the clause they wrote in Ex 6.6 and give one comment each.

D. Time to develop a habit

Ex 6.10My habit plan10 minFRAMEWORK · D3

One habit, one trigger, one date. Write it. Nobody checks it but you.

How long does a habit take to form? It varies by person and by habit. Do not trust a magic number (verify any figure you read). Plan reviews on fixed dates instead.

My habit (one sentence)
My trigger (when I will do it)
My first date and my review date
Who gives me feedback
TEACHER NOTE

Do not collect the plans. A plan written is a plan started. Ask two volunteers to read theirs aloud: the best plans have a trigger that already happens (opening a draft, sending an email).

Final mapFrom NDA to Notice on one page5 minLETTER · D4

One thing to remember about each document. Write it.

DocumentWhat I will remember
D1 NDA
Actor first, one name for each thing, a number instead of "forthwith".
D2 Joint venture
Money, risk and exit each have an article: cash calls, knock-for-knock, events of default.
Annex I Licence
It borrows the JV's law and notices; its precedence rule must agree with D2.
D3 Framework
Orders are Call-Offs; caps and delay damages decide the cost of a failure.
D4 Letter
A date, the clauses, numbered demands, a cure date and one remedy.
SAY · closing

Closing (5 minutes). "You came in with a contract and a fear of it. You leave with a method: read in seven lines, mark, organise, redraft, negotiate, edit. Keep one habit. Thank you."

Possible closing question: "Which clause would you change first in your own company's contracts, and with which of today's tools?"

How the five documents connect

D1 (NDA, Feb 2025) allows PETROX to study the data → D2 (JV, Jun 2025) with Annex I (licence) is the deal itself → D3 (Framework, Jan 2027) is signed by GER as Operator to buy from Meridian, and its cost is charged to the Joint Account → D4 (Letter, Mar 2027) enforces the NDA and Annex I C.1 through D2 11.2.

🟦 D1 · NDA (14 Feb 2025)

Objective

PETROX must be able to evaluate GER’s data (seismic data, wells, models of Blocks 14/06 and 15/07) without being able to use it for anything else. The only permitted purpose is to decide whether to sign a Joint Development Agreement.

Parties

GER (Disclosing Party) and PETROX (Receiving Party). One-way (unilateral).

Obligations of PETROX

  • Keep the information confidential (2.1).
  • Use it only for the Permitted Purpose (2.2).
  • Protect it with the same care as its own, and at least reasonable care (2.3).
  • Make its Representatives sign a “deed of confidentiality” (2.5).
  • Return or destroy the information, with a certificate (Clause 6).
  • Tell GER if an authority orders disclosure (3.1).

Rights of GER

  • Prior consent to any disclosure.
  • Choose between return and destruction.
  • Seek an injunction (7.1).
  • Terminate on 30 days’ notice (5.4).

Liability

Only the remedies clause exists. PETROX acknowledges that money is not enough and GER may “seek” an injunction. There is no cap and no agreed damages.

Dates

Term of 2 years, that is until 14 February 2027 (5.1).

Limitations

The four exceptions in 4.1: public domain, already known, independent development, received from a third party free of duty.

Discrepancies and fragile points

  • Contradictory survival. 5.2 says confidentiality lasts “in perpetuity”; 5.3 says 5 years after termination. On 18 March 2027 both rules say PETROX is still bound (for ever, or until 14 February 2032); the clash matters only after 2032.
  • Unreadable double negative in 2.4: “does not fail… would not not constitute”.
  • Circular definitions: Affiliate refers to Subsidiary and Subsidiary refers to Affiliate (1.1).
  • Clause 3.1 is circular: “subject to consent save the exceptions”.
  • No governing law and no forum. This is an important gap.
  • Data list: Schedule 1 covers data and models, not the SeismoCore software.
  • Vague deadlines: “forthwith”, “without undue delay”.
  • Notice by fax (8.4): obsolete.

🟪 D2 · Joint Development and Production Agreement (30 Jun 2025)

Objective

To exploit Blocks 14/06 and 15/07 together. GER is Operator, PETROX is Non-Operator and also receives a licence of the SeismoCore technology.

Parties

GER 60% and PETROX 40% (Participating Interests).

Obligations

  • GER: operate with diligence (8.1), keep the Joint Account in USD, issue monthly cash calls, and propose the Work Programme before 1 October (7.2).
  • PETROX: pay its share within 20 days (late interest SOFR + 3, 8.3), pay the royalty, comply with anti-corruption laws (9.3), and use the technology only in the Contract Area.

Rights

  • GER: audit the royalties (3.2) and own the intellectual property in the technology (4.1).
  • Both: cross-indemnity (knock-for-knock, Article 5) and a vote in the Operating Committee (65% needed to decide).
  • GER: prior consent if PETROX changes control (12.1).
  • Termination after an Event of Default not cured within 30 days (Article 11).

Liability

  • Loss of profit and indirect loss are excluded (10.1).
  • Cap of USD 25 million per party (10.2), with exceptions: cash calls, royalties and Article 5.
  • No limit for fraud or wilful misconduct (10.3).

Dates

Effective 30 June 2025. Cash call: 20 days. Royalty: report at 30 days and payment at 45 days after the quarter (Schedule 3). Each Calendar Quarter and calendar year. Cure period: 30 days.

Limitations

  • Licence is non-exclusive, non-transferable, not sublicensable, only in the Contract Area and only for three uses (2.2).
  • 60 days’ notice to change the multiplier.
  • Deductions limited to 20% (3.1).
  • Governing law: English law; ICC arbitration in London (Article 13).

Discrepancies and fragile points

  • Deductions: 3.1 limits them to 20% of Gross Revenue; Schedule 3 says “not subject to any percentage limit”.
  • Broken reference: 3.1 refers to “Schedule 3, Part B, Column 4”, but that Part is the reporting calendar and has no table.
  • Multiplier: GER may change it unilaterally (3.1), although 15.2 requires both signatures to amend.
  • Ownership of Derived Data: 4.2 says “equal undivided shares, subject to” three different splits (60/40, 50/50, 70/30) that overlap (a “New IP” can also be modelling).
  • Indemnity: 5.1 is reciprocal and 5.2 is one-sided (PETROX pays for injury to GER’s personnel “howsoever caused”).
  • Cross-reference: 2.1 refers to “Article 7 (Force Majeure)”, but Force Majeure is Article 6. Article 7 is the Work Programme.
  • Force majeure (Article 6): the definition is not numbered (6.1), and there is no time limit and no effect on payments.
  • Audit: the Operator decides the cost, and the Operator is GER (3.2).
  • Deadlock: with 60/40 and a 65% majority, neither GER alone (60%) nor PETROX alone (40%) can approve. Both parties are needed for every decision.
  • Duration: there is no term clause for the JV; only the Licence Term (10 years) appears in the Annex.
  • Precedence: 15.3 says the Annex prevails on the licence; Annex H.2 says the Agreement prevails. It is circular.

🟧 Annex I · Technology and Data Licence (30 Jun 2025)

Objective

To detail the licence of SeismoCore (grant, fees, support, warranties, termination). It is part of D2 and not a separate contract.

Parties

GER (licensor) and PETROX (licensee, called “Receiving Party” here).

Obligations

  • PETROX: pay the fee; use the software only on the approved infrastructure (Schedule A-2: GER’s server in Milan, access by VPN); limit access to the personnel in Exhibit A-1 (4 people); return or destroy copies within 30 days after the end.
  • GER: remote support in business hours, deliver updates and give up to 10 person-days of training.

Rights

GER may suspend access (10 days after notice of non-payment) and revoke the licence on 30 days’ notice if it determines a security risk (F.3).

Liability

Each party as set by Article 10 of D2. In addition, GER is not liable for more than the royalties paid in the previous 12 months (G.1).

Dates

Effective 30 June 2025. Licence Term: until the end of D2 or the tenth anniversary, whichever comes first (F.1), that is until 30 June 2035. Return within 30 days.

Limitations

“As is” (E.2), no warranty that the software is error-free. Licence is “limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable”. No installation outside Schedule A-2.

Discrepancies and fragile points

  • Precedence: H.2 says D2 prevails and D2 15.3 says the Annex prevails. Which one wins changes the result, for example the liability cap: USD 25M (D2 10.2) or 12 months of royalties (G.1).
  • Calculation base: the table in B.1 uses “Annual Gross Revenue” for the tiers, but B.2 says it is calculated on Net Revenue. D2 uses a flat 3.5% and the Annex uses tiers from 2.0% to 5.0%.
  • Unilateral revocation (F.3): GER decides the risk and the notice is 30 days. This clashes with D2 Article 11, where termination is only for an Event of Default.
  • Suspension: 10 days in F.2 and 30 days in D2 11.1(a).
  • Undefined term: “Seismic Data” is used in A.1 and is not defined.
  • Confidentiality (C.1): Section C.1 applies the terms of the NDA. But the NDA expired in February 2027 and its permitted purpose was to evaluate a JV (verify).

🟩 D3 · Master Collaboration and Framework Agreement (18 Jan 2027)

Objective

General rules so that GER can buy supply, logistics, installation and integration of biofuel from Meridian. Each real order is a Call-Off.

Parties

GER (as Operator of the JDA) and Meridian Offshore Systems (Contractor). Representatives: Roberto Conti for GER and James Whitfield for Meridian.

Obligations

  • Meridian: perform with professional care, use qualified personnel, comply with standards, notify within 10 Business Days to ask for more time, keep the insurance in Schedule 3 and keep records for 10 years.
  • GER: give the assigned inputs, review deliverables, and pay undisputed amounts within 60 days.

Rights

  • GER: suspend, terminate a Call-Off for convenience on 60 days’ notice, and audit records.
  • Meridian: suspend for a serious safety risk or for material non-payment after 15 days.
  • Both: terminate for material breach not cured within 30 days.

Liability

  • General cap: 100% of the Call-Off price, with a minimum of EUR 10M (16.1).
  • Separate environmental cap of EUR 20M (16.2).
  • No loss of profit (16.3).
  • Aggregate cap on delay damages: EUR 4.2M.
  • No limit for Protected Liabilities (wilful misconduct, gross negligence, etc.).

Dates

Effective 18 January 2027. Call-Off No. 1 (EUR 42M) is of the same day. Milestones: design 30 April 2027, equipment 29 October 2027, platform shutdown 10–24 May 2028, completion 31 August 2028, performance test 1–30 September 2028, Final Acceptance 31 October 2028. Warranty of 24 months.

Limitations

No minimum volume, no exclusivity and no guaranteed award (Clause 1). A Call-Off is valid only if both sign it. A purchase order or an email does not create a Call-Off (Clause 4). Delay damages are the only monetary remedy (Clause 15). Italian law and the courts of Milan (Clause 22).

Discrepancies and fragile points

  • Precedence: the Agreement prevails over the Call-Off (Clause 5). A Call-Off may depart only if it quotes the clause affected, says so expressly and is signed by someone with authority. Schedule 1 says “Approved departures: None”, but it contains two departures: a time bar for late notice and deemed acceptance of Mechanical Completion.
  • Late notice: Clause 8 limits relief only if the delay prejudices the evaluation. Schedule 1 says “is barred”, with no prejudice test.
  • Delay damages: “No termination cut-off specified”. If the EUR 4.2M cap is reached, the work can continue with no time limit.
  • Authority: Marchetti signs Change Orders and NDAs up to EUR 5M. There is no rule for larger Change Orders.
  • JV: the EUR 42M Call-Off is charged to the Joint Account, but D3 does not say that it falls within the Work Programme and Budget approved by the Operating Committee (D2 Article 7). There, GER can spend without approval only up to 10% of the budget (7.3).
  • Two legal regimes: D3 applies Italian law and Milan, and D2 applies English law and ICC London. A dispute touching both contracts can go to two forums.
  • Notices: D3 uses “confirmed receipt” and D2 uses presumed dates of receipt.
  • Cure periods: 15 days to suspend and 30 to terminate.
  • Documents that are not ours: D3 refers to an NDA of 7 September 2026 (Clause 17), a licence “HX-200” from another licensor and an RFP. They are not D1 or Annex I. Participants should read them as “references to documents we do not have”, and not work on them.
  • Link to D1: D3 does not rely on D1. It relies on a different NDA.

🟥 D4 · Letter of Notice (18 Mar 2027)

Objective

For GER to give formal notice of a material breach by PETROX and demand remedies, reserving all its rights.

Parties

From GER (signed by the Head of Legal Affairs) to the Board of Directors of PETROX.

Obligations it imposes (on PETROX)

  • (i) cease immediately;
  • (ii) give a written explanation of what was disclosed;
  • (iii) obtain the return or destruction by third parties;
  • (iv) pay damages, with no amount stated.

Rights GER claims

Injunction, specific performance, damages and legal proceedings, with no waiver of anything.

Liability

It states no figure. Damages are reserved (“quantum… expressly reserved”).

Dates

18 March 2027. It gives no deadline of its own: “forthwith”, “within a period to be determined by GER”, “within a reasonable time”.

Limitations

It does not mention or quote any cure period.

Discrepancies and fragile points

  • Expired NDA: the NDA term ended on 14 February 2027, a month before the letter, but confidentiality survives under both 5.2 (for ever) and 5.3 (five years, until 14 February 2032), so PETROX is still bound. The real gaps are: the letter gives no date for the disclosure, and the software (SeismoCore) is not listed in the NDA’s Schedule 1, so GER should also rely on Annex I C.1 and D2 (verify).
  • It does not follow the D2 procedure. 11.2 requires a statement that it is a notice under 11.2, the provision breached, the facts and the 30-day cure period. The letter quotes no D2 clause. 14.1 also requires delivery by courier; the letter goes by registered post and email. 14.3 names the Company Secretary and the letter goes to the Board. Result: no Event of Default is reached and termination is not possible (verify).
  • Wrong citation: “Article C.1” where it is Section C.1. And C.1 creates no new duty: it only refers to the NDA.
  • Doubtful scope: the letter accuses PETROX of disclosing “SeismoCore specifications” and “Derived Data”. The NDA list (Schedule 1) does not include the software. And D2 4.2 gives PETROX between 30% and 50% of the Derived Data, so it is not clearly GER’s information.
  • Forum: it threatens “legal proceedings”, but D2 Article 13 sends disputes to ICC arbitration in London. The NDA has no forum.
  • Language: archaisms (“heretofore”, “aforesaid”, “to wit”, “forthwith”), which Exercise 5.11 turns into modern wording.

Discrepancies across several contracts

  1. Precedence: D2 15.3 against Annex I H.2.
  2. Length of confidentiality: NDA 5.2 against 5.3 (both keep the duty alive on 18 March 2027; they differ only after 14 February 2032), and the NDA term ended on 14 February 2027.
  3. Law and forum: the NDA has none; D2 and the Annex are English law with ICC London; D3 is Italian law with Milan.
  4. Non-payment or suspension periods: 10 days (Annex I), 30 days (D2), 15 days (D3).
  5. Liability caps: USD 25M (D2), 12 months of royalties (Annex I), 100% of the price with a minimum of EUR 10M (D3).
  6. Who signs: Paolo Ricci, Head of E&P Division, signs D1 and D2. In D3, Schedule 2 says Conti signs the Framework and the Licence and Marchetti signs NDAs. It is worth verifying whether Ricci had authority to sign D1 and D2.

Classroom tip

For the classroom, the most valuable points to teach are the precedence clash (Ex 5.9), the length of confidentiality (Ex 5.9) and the letter (D4 against D2 11.2, Ex 5.11 and 5.12). All three connect with clauses that participants can redraft in the exercises.

GER / PETROX — Joint Development

THIS CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT (hereinafter referred to as the 'Agreement', 'this Agreement', or 'the NDA'), is made and entered into as of this 14th day of February 2025, (hereinafter the 'Effective Date'), by and between the following parties:

GLOBAL ENERGY RESOURCES S.p.A., a company duly organised and existing under the laws of the Republic of Italy, having its principal place of business at Via Cesare Pavese 14, 20138 Milan (MI), Italy, acting through its Exploration & Production Division (hereinafter referred to as 'Disclosing Party', 'GER', 'the Company', or 'Owner' as the context may from time to time require and as more particularly described herein and in the schedules and annexes hereto);

AND

PETROX INTERNATIONAL LIMITED, a company incorporated pursuant to the Companies Act 2006 of England and Wales, having its registered office at 88 Cannon Street, London EC4N 6JJ, United Kingdom, (hereinafter referred to as 'Receiving Party', 'PETROX', 'the Partner', or 'Recipient' as the context may from time to time require, such terms being used interchangeably throughout this Agreement);

GER and PETROX are hereinafter referred to individually as a 'Party' and collectively as the 'Parties'.

RECITALS

WHEREAS, GER is the holder and registered owner of certain proprietary technical and geological data, subsurface models, seismic datasets, geophysical interpretations, well data, and other information relating to Blocks 14/06 and 15/07 of the Central Adriatic Basin, as more particularly described in Schedule 1 hereto and as may be amended by GER from time to time at its absolute and unfettered discretion (hereinafter referred to as 'the Confidential Information', and the definition of which shall be deemed to incorporate, by reference, any and all information of a confidential or proprietary nature whether or not expressly marked as such);

WHEREAS, PETROX has expressed a desire and an intention to evaluate the Confidential Information for the sole and exclusive purpose of determining whether it wishes to enter into a Joint Development Agreement or similar commercial arrangement with GER in relation to the aforementioned Blocks (hereinafter referred to as 'the Permitted Purpose', 'the Evaluation Purpose', or 'the Agreed Purpose', such terms being used interchangeably throughout this Agreement, notwithstanding that 'Permitted Purpose' shall govern in all cases of conflict);

WHEREAS, it is desired by both Parties that the Confidential Information shall be disclosed by GER to PETROX upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement, which shall be binding upon the Parties, their respective successors, permitted assigns, employees, contractors, and agents;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants, promises, undertakings, and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, THE PARTIES HEREBY AGREE AS FOLLOWS:

CLAUSE 1 — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION

1.1 In this Agreement, the following words and expressions shall have the following meanings as more particularly set out below, unless the context shall otherwise require or unless otherwise specifically defined elsewhere in this Agreement:

(a) "Affiliate" shall mean any entity that, directly or indirectly, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a Party, whereby 'control' shall be construed in accordance with the provisions of sub-clause 1.1(a)(i) hereof, and the definition of 'Affiliate' shall be deemed to include any Subsidiary as defined in sub-clause 1.1(b) below;

(b) "Subsidiary" shall mean any entity that constitutes a controlled Affiliate of a Party pursuant to the definition set out in sub-clause 1.1(a) above and the control thresholds specified therein;

(c) "Confidential Information" means and includes, without limitation, all information, data, materials, documents, specifications, formulae, processes, designs, concepts, technical know-how, trade secrets, business plans, financial projections, geological and geophysical data, seismic interpretations, well logs, reservoir models, maps, reports, analyses, and all other information disclosed or made available by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party in connection with the Permitted Purpose, whether disclosed in writing, orally, electronically, visually, or by any other means, and whether or not specifically identified or marked as 'Confidential', PROVIDED ALWAYS THAT Confidential Information shall not include information falling within any of the exceptions in Clause 4 hereof;

(d) "Representatives" shall mean the Receiving Party's officers, directors, employees, professional advisors, agents, and contractors who have a need to know the Confidential Information for the Permitted Purpose and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality no less restrictive than those contained herein, and shall include any Subsidiary or Affiliate as defined in sub-clauses 1.1(a) and 1.1(b) above;

1.2 Interpretation. In this Agreement, unless the context otherwise requires: (i) references to one gender shall include all genders; (ii) references to the singular shall include the plural and vice versa; (iii) references to a 'Clause' or 'sub-clause' shall be references to a clause or sub-clause of this Agreement; (iv) the word 'including' shall not be construed restrictively but shall mean 'including without limitation'; (v) references to any statute or statutory provision shall include any amendment thereto in force from time to time; and (vi) the headings in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect its construction or interpretation.

CLAUSE 2 — OBLIGATIONS OF THE RECEIVING PARTY

2.1 The Confidential Information shall be received and held by the Receiving Party in strict confidence. The Confidential Information shall not be disclosed, divulged, communicated, or revealed to any third party without the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party having first been obtained.

2.2 It is acknowledged that the Confidential Information shall only be used by the Receiving Party for the Permitted Purpose and for no other purpose whatsoever.

2.3 The Receiving Party undertakes to ensure that the Confidential Information shall at all times be kept and maintained in a secure manner, using not less than the same degree of care as the Receiving Party applies to its own confidential information, and in any event not less than a reasonable degree of care.

2.4 The Receiving Party shall not be under any obligation not to use any information that, were it not for the fact that it does not fail to meet the criteria set forth in Clause 4, would not not constitute Confidential Information.

2.5 The Receiving Party shall procure that each of its Representatives to whom Confidential Information is disclosed shall, prior to such disclosure, execute and deliver to the Disclosing Party a deed of confidentiality in form and substance satisfactory to the Disclosing Party, acting reasonably.

CLAUSE 3 — PERMITTED DISCLOSURE

3.1 Notwithstanding the provisions of Clause 2, and subject always to the prior written consent of the Disclosing Party save in respect of the exceptions hereinafter provided, the Receiving Party shall, and shall procure that its Representatives shall, be entitled to disclose Confidential Information in circumstances where such disclosure is required by any court of competent jurisdiction, or any governmental, quasi-governmental, regulatory, or supervisory authority, body, or agency having authority over the Receiving Party or any of its Affiliates, or pursuant to any applicable law, regulation, rule, or order, including but not limited to any stock exchange listing requirement or rule, provided always that, to the extent not prohibited by applicable law, the Receiving Party shall, forthwith upon becoming aware of any such requirement, furnish written notice to the Disclosing Party with such notice to include the full nature and scope of the required disclosure and the identity of the relevant authority, such notice to be provided in sufficient time to permit the Disclosing Party to seek a protective order or other appropriate relief, and the Receiving Party shall, in any event, co-operate fully with the Disclosing Party in its efforts to resist any such disclosure and shall disclose only such Confidential Information as is strictly required by the applicable law, regulation, or court order.

CLAUSE 4 — EXCEPTIONS TO CONFIDENTIALITY

4.1 The obligations of confidentiality set forth in Clause 2 hereof shall not apply to any information which:

(a) at the time of disclosure hereunder is, or thereafter becomes, part of the public domain otherwise than through the act or omission of the Receiving Party or its Representatives in breach of this Agreement or any other obligation of confidence; or

(b) was in the Receiving Party's possession, free of any obligation of confidence, prior to the time of disclosure hereunder, as evidenced by written records predating such disclosure; or

(c) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to, and without use of, any of the Confidential Information; or

(d) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party who, to the Receiving Party's reasonable knowledge, is free of any restriction as to its disclosure.

CLAUSE 5 — TERM AND TERMINATION

5.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of two (2) years therefrom unless sooner terminated in accordance with the provisions hereof (the 'Term').

5.2 Notwithstanding the foregoing, the confidentiality obligations undertaken by the Receiving Party pursuant to Clause 2 hereof shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement and shall remain binding upon the Receiving Party in perpetuity.

5.3 The Receiving Party's obligations of confidentiality hereunder shall, following the termination or expiry of this Agreement, continue to bind the Receiving Party for a period of five (5) years from the date of such termination or expiry.

5.4 Either Party may, at any time, terminate this Agreement upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Party;

CLAUSE 6 — RETURN OR DESTRUCTION OF INFORMATION

6.1 Forthwith upon the earlier of: (a) the termination or expiry of this Agreement; or (b) the receipt by the Receiving Party of written demand therefor from the Disclosing Party; or (c) the Receiving Party's determination that the Confidential Information is no longer required for the Permitted Purpose — the Receiving Party shall, without undue delay and at the Disclosing Party's election, either return to the Disclosing Party all Confidential Information (including all copies, extracts, summaries, and derivatives thereof) or destroy the same by secure means, and in the event of destruction, shall forthwith provide a certificate of destruction executed by a duly authorised officer of the Receiving Party.

CLAUSE 7 — REMEDIES

7.1 The Receiving Party hereby acknowledges and agrees that money damages alone would be an inadequate remedy for any breach of the obligations undertaken herein, and that, in the event of any breach or threatened breach of this Agreement by the Receiving Party, the Disclosing Party shall be entitled, in addition to and without prejudice to all other rights and remedies available to it, whether at law or in equity, to seek injunctive or other equitable relief.

CLAUSE 8 — GENERAL PROVISIONS

8.1 This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, warranties, undertakings, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating thereto.

8.2 This Agreement may not be amended or modified except by written instrument duly executed by authorised signatories of each of the Parties.

8.3 Neither Party shall assign, transfer, novate, or otherwise dispose of any of its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the other Party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed, or conditioned.

8.4 Any notice required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given if delivered personally, or sent by registered post or nationally recognised courier service, or by facsimile transmission with written confirmation, to the address set forth in the preamble hereof or to such other address as a Party may designate in writing from time to time.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

ARTICLE 1 — DEFINITIONS

As used herein, and in addition to the terms defined elsewhere in this Agreement and in the Technology License Annex attached hereto as Annex I (which is hereby incorporated into and forms an integral part of this Agreement), the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below:

"Agreement" means this Joint Development and Production Agreement together with all Schedules, Exhibits, and Annexes attached hereto or incorporated herein by reference, as the same may be amended from time to time by written agreement of the Parties in accordance with the provisions hereof.

"Joint Account" means the account to be maintained by the Operator in which shall be recorded all costs, expenses, liabilities, credits, revenues, and receipts attributable to Joint Operations pursuant to and in accordance with the Accounting Procedure set forth in Schedule 2 hereto.

"Joint Operations" means all activities, operations, works, and services carried out, or caused to be carried out, jointly by or on behalf of the Parties in connection with the exploration for, appraisal, development, and production of Petroleum from the Contract Area, pursuant to and in conformity with the Work Programme and Budget approved in accordance with Article 6 hereof.

"Petroleum" means crude oil, condensate, natural gas, natural gas liquids, and all other hydrocarbons and associated substances produced from or attributable to the Contract Area, whether in liquid or gaseous form at the wellhead.

"Licensed Technology" means the SeismoCoreTM seismic data processing and interpretation software platform, version 7.2 and any subsequent update, patch, or enhancement thereto released by GER during the term hereof, including all associated algorithms, source code (to the extent provided), object code, user documentation, and technical manuals, as more particularly described in Annex I hereto.

"Business Day" means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in London or Milan.

"Calendar Quarter" means each period of three months ending on 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December; "Calendar Year" means a period of twelve months beginning on 1 January.

"Contract Area" means the area covered by Blocks 14/06 and 15/07 of the Central Adriatic Basin, as delineated in Schedule 1.

"Intellectual Property" means patents, copyright, database rights, know-how, trade secrets and all other intellectual property rights, whether registered or not.

"Operating Committee" means the committee established under Article 7.

"Participating Interest" means, for GER, sixty percent (60%) and, for PETROX, forty percent (40%).

"Permitted Field Operations" means seismic data processing, subsurface modelling and reservoir characterisation carried out for the Joint Operations.

ARTICLE 2 — GRANT OF LICENCE AND TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER

2.1 Subject to and conditional upon the due and timely payment by the Licensee of all fees, royalties, and other amounts payable hereunder, and provided always that no Event of Default (as defined in Article 11) shall have occurred and be continuing, and save where the provisions of Article 7 (Force Majeure) shall apply, it is hereby agreed that a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence to use the Licensed Technology within the Contract Area for the Permitted Field Operations during the Licence Term shall be granted by GER to PETROX.

2.2 The licence granted pursuant to Clause 2.1 above shall, notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, be strictly limited to use of the Licensed Technology for the purposes of seismic data processing, subsurface modelling, and reservoir characterisation operations conducted exclusively within the boundaries of the Contract Area as delineated in Schedule 1 hereto, and shall not extend to, nor shall be deemed to authorise, any use of the Licensed Technology for any other purpose, including but not limited to any comparative study, benchmarking exercise, or data extraction activity, the whole of which are hereby expressly prohibited and excluded from the scope of the licence hereby granted.

ARTICLE 3 — ROYALTY STRUCTURE AND PAYMENT MECHANISM

3.1 In consideration of the licence granted hereunder, the Licensee shall pay to the Licensor a royalty calculated as follows:

Base Royalty Rate: Three and one-half percent (3.5%) of Net Revenue attributable to production from wells in which the Licensed Technology was utilised in any phase of exploration, appraisal, or development operations, less and except any amounts attributable to third-party costs incurred by the Licensee in connection with the deployment of the Licensed Technology, provided that such deductions shall not in any event exceed twenty percent (20%) of the Gross Revenue generated from the relevant wells in any given Calendar Quarter, adjusted upwards or downwards in accordance with the Production Volume Multiplier Table set forth in Schedule 3, Part B, Column 4, as may from time to time be amended by GER upon sixty (60) days' written notice to PETROX.

3.2 The Licensor shall have the right, exercisable upon not less than five (5) Business Days' written notice to the Licensee, to audit the Licensee's books and records for the purposes of verifying royalty calculations hereunder; provided, however, that such audit rights shall not be exercised more than once per Calendar Year; provided further that any discrepancy of less than two percent (2%) of the aggregate royalty amounts payable in the period under audit shall not give rise to any obligation to correct or adjust such amounts; and provided further that the costs of any such audit shall be borne by the party that bears the greater burden of the audit, the determination of which shall be made by the Operator acting reasonably.

ARTICLE 4 — INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DATA OWNERSHIP

4.1 All Intellectual Property rights in and to the Licensed Technology shall remain vested in and the absolute property of GER, and nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer, assign, or convey any Intellectual Property right to PETROX.

4.2 All data, results, interpretations, and derivative works created by PETROX in the course of using the Licensed Technology ('Derived Data') shall be jointly owned by the Parties in equal undivided shares, subject to the following allocation:

(a) Derived Data relating to raw seismic processing outputs shall be owned sixty percent (60%) by GER and forty percent (40%) by PETROX;

(b) Derived Data relating to reservoir modelling and characterisation shall be owned fifty percent (50%) by each Party;

(c) Derived Data that constitutes a novel discovery, methodology, or process (' New IP') shall be owned seventy percent (70%) by GER and thirty percent (30%) by PETROX.

ARTICLE 5 — INDEMNIFICATION AND KNOCK-FOR-KNOCK

5.1 Each Party shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the other Party, its Affiliates, and its and their respective officers, directors, employees, contractors, and agents (collectively, 'Indemnitees') from and against any and all claims, actions, demands, losses, damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable legal fees) arising out of or in connection with:

(a) any bodily injury to or death of any person employed by or contracted to the Indemnifying Party; and

(b) any loss of or damage to the property of the Indemnifying Party; regardless of the negligence (whether sole, concurrent, gross, or otherwise) or breach of duty of any Indemnitee.

5.2 Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, PETROX shall indemnify, defend, and hold GER harmless from and against any and all claims, actions, demands, losses, damages, liabilities, and expenses arising out of or in connection with any bodily injury to, or death of, any employee, contractor, or agent of GER or any GER Affiliate, howsoever caused.

ARTICLE 6 — FORCE MAJEURE

"Force Majeure Event" shall mean any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party, including without limitation: acts of God, fires, floods, earthquakes, epidemics, wars (whether declared or undeclared), acts of terrorism, civil disturbances, sabotage, government actions, embargoes, blockades, labour disputes, strikes, and any other events of a similar nature or character.

6.2 If a Force Majeure Event occurs, the affected Party shall be relieved of its obligations under this Agreement to the extent that performance of such obligations is prevented or delayed by the Force Majeure Event.

6.3 The affected Party shall give notice of the Force Majeure Event to the other Party as soon as reasonably practicable.

ARTICLE 7 — WORK PROGRAMME AND BUDGET

7.1 The Operating Committee consists of two representatives of each Party. A decision of the Operating Committee requires the affirmative vote of Parties holding at least sixty-five percent (65%) of the Participating Interests.

7.2 The Operator shall submit a proposed Work Programme and Budget for each Calendar Year not later than 1 October of the preceding year. The Operating Committee shall approve the proposal or give written comments within thirty (30) days.

7.3 The Operator may incur unbudgeted expenditure of up to ten percent (10%) of the approved budget for a Calendar Year, and any expenditure needed to protect persons, property or the environment in an emergency.

ARTICLE 8 — OPERATORSHIP, JOINT ACCOUNT AND CASH CALLS

8.1 GER is the Operator and shall conduct the Joint Operations diligently and in accordance with good international oilfield practice.

8.2 The Operator shall keep the Joint Account in United States dollars in accordance with Schedule 2.

8.3 The Operator shall issue cash calls monthly. Each Party shall pay its Participating Interest share within twenty (20) days after receipt of the cash call. Late payments bear interest at three (3) percentage points above the secured overnight financing rate (SOFR).

ARTICLE 9 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES

9.1 Each Party represents that it has the capacity and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement.

9.2 GER represents that it has the right to license the Licensed Technology to PETROX. GER does not warrant that the Licensed Technology or its outputs are free from error or fit for any particular purpose.

9.3 Each Party represents that it complies with applicable anti-bribery laws, including Legislative Decree 231/2001 and the UK Bribery Act 2010.

ARTICLE 10 — LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

10.1 Neither Party is liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, or for loss of production, profit or revenue.

10.2 The aggregate liability of each Party to the other under this Agreement and Annex I, other than for payment of cash calls and royalties and under Article 5, is limited to USD 25,000,000.

10.3 Nothing in this Agreement limits liability for fraud or wilful misconduct.

ARTICLE 11 — EVENTS OF DEFAULT AND TERMINATION

11.1 Each of the following is an Event of Default by a Party (the Defaulting Party): (a) failure to pay an amount due under this Agreement within thirty (30) days after written notice of non-payment; (b) a material breach of this Agreement or Annex I that is not remedied within thirty (30) days after the other Party gives written notice specifying the breach in reasonable detail and the remedy required; or (c) the Defaulting Party becomes insolvent or enters into liquidation.

11.2 A notice under Clause 11.1(b) must be given in accordance with Article 14, must state that it is a notice under this Clause 11.2, must identify the provision breached and the facts relied on, and must state the cure period.

11.3 If an Event of Default continues after the cure period, the other Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice with immediate effect.

11.4 On termination, the licence granted under Article 2 and Annex I ends, accrued rights remain, and Articles 5, 10 and 13 survive.

ARTICLE 12 — ASSIGNMENT

12.1 Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. A change of control of PETROX requires GER's prior written consent.

ARTICLE 13 — GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

13.1 This Agreement, Annex I and any non-contractual obligations arising out of them are governed by English law.

13.2 Any dispute arising out of this Agreement or Annex I shall be finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by three arbitrators. The seat is London and the language is English.

13.3 Either Party may apply to a competent court for urgent interim relief. A dispute about the Joint Account may be referred to an independent accounting expert.

ARTICLE 14 — NOTICES

14.1 A notice must be in writing in English and delivered by hand, by international courier or by email to the address in Clause 14.3. A notice under Clause 11.2 or of termination must also be sent by courier.

14.2 A notice is deemed received: if delivered by hand, on delivery; if sent by courier, on the second Business Day after dispatch; if sent by email, on the next Business Day after sending, unless the sender receives a delivery-failure message.

14.3 Addresses: GER: Via Cesare Pavese 14, 20138 Milan (MI), Italy; Attention: Head of Legal Affairs, Exploration & Production Division; legal.ep@ger-energy.example. PETROX: 88 Cannon Street, London EC4N 6JJ, United Kingdom; Attention: The Company Secretary; legal@petrox-intl.example.

ARTICLE 15 — GENERAL PROVISIONS

15.1 This Agreement, its Schedules and Annex I are the entire agreement of the Parties on their subject matter.

15.2 An amendment must be in writing and signed by authorised signatories of both Parties.

15.3 If this Agreement and Annex I conflict on a matter concerning the licence, Annex I prevails.

15.4 A person who is not a Party has no right to enforce this Agreement under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999.

15.5 A failure to enforce a right is not a waiver. If a provision is invalid, the rest of this Agreement continues in force. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts.

SCHEDULE 3 — NET REVENUE AND PERMITTED DEDUCTIONS

Part A — Definitions

"Net Revenue" means Gross Revenue less Permitted Deductions.

"Permitted Deductions" means: (a) costs of transporting and processing Petroleum to the point of sale; (b) taxes and government royalties; (c) third-party costs incurred by the Licensee in deploying the Licensed Technology; and (d) the Operator's overhead charged to the Joint Account. Permitted Deductions are not subject to any percentage limit.

Part B — Reporting

The Licensee shall deliver a royalty statement within thirty (30) days after the end of each Calendar Quarter and shall pay the royalty shown within forty-five (45) days after the end of that Calendar Quarter.

1. Purpose and Contracting Model

This Agreement establishes the contractual framework for collaboration, supply, logistics, integration and related services for Project Horizon.

GER enters into this Agreement as Operator under the JDA. The Contract Price of each Call-Off is charged to the Joint Account.

The Parties MUST perform their expressly allocated obligations under this Agreement and each effective Call-Off.

This Agreement creates no minimum purchase volume, exclusivity or guaranteed award.

Neither Party has authority to bind the other. The expression “collaboration” does not create a separate legal partnership or joint venture.

2. Definitions

Business Day means a day other than Saturday, Sunday or a public holiday in Milan.

Call-Off means an order signed under Clause 4.

Change Order means a signed amendment identifying a change to a Call-Off.

Contract Price means the price stated in the relevant Call-Off, adjusted by signed Change Orders.

Deliverables means the items expressly identified in a Call-Off.

Protected Liabilities means fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence and other liabilities that applicable law does not permit the Parties to exclude or limit.

SOW means the statement of work incorporated into a Call-Off.

3. Governance and Cooperation

Each Party MUST appoint a contract representative and a project representative.

Contract representatives manage contractual changes, notices and escalations. Project representatives manage day-to-day coordination within their delegated authority.

Each Party MUST:

provide agreed inputs on time;

identify material risks promptly;

cooperate on interfaces;

maintain accurate project records;

avoid knowingly issuing instructions inconsistent with the Contract Documents.

A governance meeting does not itself amend the contract.

4. Call-Off Formation

Either Party MAY propose a Call-Off.

A Call-Off WILL become effective only when signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.

Each Call-Off MUST identify:

scope and exclusions;

Deliverables;

price and taxes;

payment milestones;

programme;

acceptance criteria;

GER dependencies;

subcontractors;

applicable warranties;

delay damages;

insurance requirements;

any approved contractual departures.

A quotation, purchase order, acknowledgement or routine email does not by itself create a Call-Off under this procedure.

The Contractor MUST NOT begin chargeable work without an effective Call-Off or separate signed early-work authorisation.

5. Order of Precedence

If Contract Documents conflict, the following order WILL apply:

a signed amendment expressly identifying the provisions changed;

this Agreement;

the signed Call-Off;

its incorporated SOW;

technical schedules;

other expressly incorporated documents.

A lower-ranking document MAY override this Agreement only if it:

identifies the affected clause;

expressly states the intended override;

identifies the affected Call-Off;

is signed by representatives authorised to approve that departure.

An approved departure applies only to the identified Call-Off unless expressly stated otherwise.

Supplier standard terms are excluded unless expressly incorporated through this procedure.

A technical specification does not change liability, intellectual property, governing law or dispute resolution merely because it is more detailed.

An incorporated Technology Licence Agreement will govern the specifically identified technology rights. The Parties MUST identify any departures it makes from this Agreement in the approved-departures register.

6. Performance Standard

The Contractor MUST:

perform the Work with the agreed professional care and competence;

provide suitably qualified personnel;

comply with agreed specifications;

comply with laws applicable to its activities;

maintain required permits within its allocated responsibility;

use materials and equipment meeting the agreed specifications;

manage approved subcontractors.

The Contractor MUST notify GER promptly if an instruction would create a safety risk, breach applicable law or conflict with an agreed technical requirement.

7. GER Inputs and Site Access

GER MUST provide the inputs and access expressly allocated to it in the relevant Call-Off.

The Contractor MUST review provided information for reasonably identifiable inconsistencies and notify GER promptly.

The Contractor does not assume responsibility for the accuracy of GER-controlled data merely by receiving it.

A failure to identify an inconsistency does not transfer every associated risk to the Contractor; responsibility remains governed by the express allocation and the Contractor’s agreed review duty.

8. Programme and Time Relief

The Contractor MUST maintain an updated programme and promptly notify GER of events affecting completion.

A time-relief claim MUST identify:

the event;

contractual basis;

affected activities;

estimated impact;

supporting records;

mitigation.

The Contractor MUST notify GER within 10 Business Days after becoming aware of the event.

A late notice will affect relief only to the extent expressly agreed in the Call-Off and the delay prejudices assessment or mitigation.

GER WILL assess a properly supported claim within 15 Business Days.

Approved relief WILL be recorded through a programme adjustment or Change Order.

No automatic price increase follows from a time extension unless expressly agreed.

9. Changes

A change request MUST state its effect on scope, price, programme, testing and risk allocation.

Neither Party is obliged to implement a proposed commercial change before signature.

For an immediate safety measure, the Contractor MUST take reasonable protective action and notify GER promptly. The Parties WILL then assess the contractual consequences without treating the emergency action as automatic acceptance of a price adjustment.

10. Delivery and Acceptance

The Contractor MUST deliver according to the agreed delivery terms and location.

Each Call-Off MUST specify when title and risk transfer. Physical receipt does not itself constitute final acceptance.

GER MUST review submitted Deliverables within the agreed review period.

A rejection MUST identify the unmet acceptance criteria.

The Contractor MUST correct attributable non-conformities and resubmit the affected Deliverable.

Acceptance does not waive latent defects, fraud or expressly surviving warranties.

Deemed acceptance applies only if expressly included in the Call-Off, with its trigger and consequences clearly identified.

11. Prices, Invoices and Payment

Prices are those stated in the Call-Off.

The Contractor MUST submit invoices with the agreed milestone evidence and supporting records.

GER MUST pay undisputed amounts within 60 days after receiving a valid invoice.

GER MUST identify disputed amounts and reasons promptly. The Parties MUST continue processing undisputed amounts.

The Contractor MUST obtain prior approval for reimbursable expenditure where the Call-Off requires approval.

Neither Party MAY set off a genuinely disputed amount unless permitted by an express contractual provision or applicable law.

12. Warranties and Defects

The Contractor warrants that its Deliverables meet the agreed specifications and acceptance criteria.

The warranty period is 24 months from the event identified in the Call-Off.

For an attributable defect notified during that period, the Contractor MUST repair, replace or reperform within a reasonable period agreed by reference to the defect’s operational significance.

If the Contractor fails to act after reasonable notice, GER MAY procure reasonable corrective work and recover attributable, documented costs subject to Section 16.

This warranty does not cover defects caused solely by unauthorised modification, misuse or GER inputs outside agreed specifications.

13. Sustainability and Environmental Obligations

Each Call-Off involving biofuel MUST identify:

the relevant feedstock and intended use;

applicable sustainability criteria;

carbon-intensity methodology;

supporting evidence;

the party responsible for each data set;

verification and record-retention requirements.

The responsible supplying Party MUST provide accurate, complete and traceable information within its allocated scope.

The Contractor MUST promptly report environmental incidents arising from its Work, take reasonable containment measures and preserve relevant evidence.

14. Environmental Indemnity

The Contractor MUST reimburse GER for reasonable, documented investigation, containment and clean-up costs and third-party claims to the extent caused by:

contaminated materials supplied by the Contractor; or

the Contractor’s breach of agreed environmental handling obligations.

The indemnity does not cover the portion caused by GER’s subsequent handling or another party’s conduct for which the Contractor is not responsible.

GER MAY take immediate reasonable protective action without awaiting approval.

GER MUST provide prompt notice and reasonable supporting evidence.

The Contractor MAY participate in investigations and third-party defence. Neither Party MAY impose obligations or admissions on the other through a settlement without its written consent.

Mixed-cause losses WILL be allocated according to each Party’s contribution.

15. Delay Damages

Delay damages apply only to milestones, rates and caps expressly identified in a Call-Off.

They WILL accrue against adjusted milestone dates.

Unless the Call-Off expressly provides otherwise, delay damages are the sole monetary remedy for the relevant milestone delay, subject to Protected Liabilities.

GER MUST NOT recover twice for the same loss.

Reaching a delay-damages cap does not automatically terminate the Call-Off.

16. Liability Allocation

16.1 General cap

Each Party’s aggregate ordinary liability under this Agreement and the Call-Offs is capped at:

For each Call-Off, 100 per cent. of the Contract Price of that Call-Off, subject to a minimum of EUR 10,000,000, applying over the life of the Call-Off including its warranty period.

16.2 Environmental cap

Ordinary liability under Clause 14 is subject to a separate aggregate cap of EUR 20,000,000.

That cap is separate from, and does not consume, the general cap.

16.3 Excluded commercial losses

Subject to Clauses 16.4 and 16.5, neither Party is liable to the other for loss of profit, revenue, production, use or business opportunity, whether characterised as direct or indirect.

16.4 Express recoverable amounts

The exclusions do not exclude:

agreed delay damages;

reasonable defect correction and substitute-procurement costs;

amounts recoverable under the environmental indemnity;

agreed confidentiality incident costs.

Those amounts remain subject to their applicable caps.

16.5 Protected Liabilities

No cap, loss exclusion, exclusive-remedy provision or other contractual limitation applies to Protected Liabilities.

16.6 Payment and duplication

Accrued contractual payment obligations are not reduced by the liability cap.

A Party MUST NOT recover twice for the same loss.

16.7 Subcontractors

Each Party remains responsible for personnel and subcontractors it uses to perform its obligations. Allocating activities among Call-Offs does not create additional caps unless expressly agreed.

17. Intellectual Property and Confidentiality

Each Party retains its pre-existing intellectual property.

Each Call-Off MUST identify ownership and permitted use of project-specific Deliverables.

GER’s payment for services does not itself transfer proprietary technology rights.

Confidential information remains subject to the NDA dated 7 September 2026. This Agreement does not extinguish accrued NDA rights.

18. Insurance and Records

The Contractor MUST maintain the insurance identified in Schedule 3.

Insurance does not replace contractual obligations or enlarge an agreed liability cap.

Each Party MUST retain records needed to verify performance, invoicing and allocated sustainability obligations for 10 years after Final Acceptance of the relevant Call-Off.

GER MAY audit relevant records on reasonable notice, subject to confidentiality, security and protection of unrelated information.

19. Suspension

GER MAY suspend affected Work by written notice stating its scope and reason.

The Contractor MUST protect completed Work and minimise reasonable suspension costs.

The consequences of a GER-directed suspension not caused by Contractor breach WILL be assessed through change control.

The Contractor MAY suspend affected Work for a serious safety risk or a material overdue undisputed payment after the notice and cure period of 15 days.

20. Termination

Either Party MAY terminate an affected Call-Off for material breach not remedied within 30 days after written notice, or sooner where the breach cannot reasonably be remedied.

GER MAY terminate a Call-Off for convenience on 60 days’ notice.

On convenience termination, GER MUST pay for:

conforming Work performed;

approved, non-cancellable commitments;

reasonable documented demobilisation costs;

less avoided costs and amounts already paid.

No profit on unperformed Work is payable unless expressly agreed.

Termination of this Agreement does not automatically terminate existing Call-Offs. The termination notice MUST identify the intended effect.

On termination, the Parties MUST arrange delivery of paid-for Deliverables, return of property and protection of Confidential Information.

21. Events Beyond Reasonable Control

A Party affected by an event beyond its reasonable control that prevents performance MUST notify the other promptly, explain the effect and take reasonable mitigation measures.

Relief applies only to affected obligations and periods.

Payment for completed performance is not excused.

If the event continues for 90 days, either Party MAY terminate the materially affected Call-Off by notice.

22. General and Dispute Provisions

Amendments MUST be signed by authorised representatives.

Neither Party MAY assign this Agreement without prior written consent.

Formal notices MUST be sent to the addresses in Schedule 4 and WILL take effect on confirmed receipt.

Italian law governs this Agreement and the Call-Offs.

The Parties MUST escalate disputes to senior representatives for 20 Business Days before commencing ordinary proceedings.

The competent courts of Milan have exclusive jurisdiction, without preventing an application for urgent protective relief.

Dear Sirs,

We write to you heretofore and hereinafter in respect of certain matters which have recently come to the attention of Global Energy Resources S.p.A. (hereinafter referred to as 'GER' or 'our client' or 'the Aggrieved Party') concerning the actions, omissions, and conduct of PETROX International Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'PETROX' or 'you' or 'your organisation' or 'the Defaulting Party') which, GER avers and contends, constitute a material breach of the Relevant Agreements.

It has come to the attention of GER that, notwithstanding the express obligations of confidentiality and restricted use undertaken by PETROX pursuant to the terms of the aforegoing NDA and the Annex I Licence Agreement, PETROX has, without the knowledge, consent, or authorisation of GER, and in direct and flagrant contravention of its obligations thereunder, disclosed, divulged, communicated, or caused to be disclosed certain Confidential Information, to wit, aspects of the SeismoCoreTM Licensed Technology specifications and certain Derived Data outputs, to third parties, the identity of whom is as yet not fully known to GER.

GER hereby puts PETROX on formal notice that the aforesaid conduct constitutes, in GER's considered opinion and on legal advice, a material breach of the Relevant Agreements, and GER hereby demands forthwith, and not later than such time as may be reasonably practicable in all the circumstances, that PETROX:

(i) Cease and desist forthwith from any further disclosure, use, or exploitation of the Confidential Information or the Licensed Technology for any purpose other than as expressly permitted under the Relevant Agreements;

(ii) Provide GER with a full and unqualified written account, verified by statutory declaration, of all disclosures made, to whom, and in what form, within a period to be determined by GER;

(iii) Procure the immediate return or certified destruction of all Confidential Information disclosed to any third party, to the extent that such procurement is within PETROX's power;

(iv) Pay to GER such damages, losses, costs, and expenses as GER may suffer or incur as a consequence of the said breach, the quantum of which is expressly reserved.

GER further reserves all rights and remedies available to it at law or in equity, including but not limited to the right to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and damages for breach of contract, and nothing herein shall be construed as a waiver of any such rights.

GER trusts that PETROX will take all necessary and appropriate steps to remedy the aforesaid breach in accordance with the terms of this notice. Should PETROX fail to comply with the demands herein within a reasonable time, GER reserves the right to take such further steps, including the commencement of legal proceedings, as it may deem necessary and appropriate in the circumstances.
